items.evidence: The acceptance AC#1 test passes and asserts street, toAct===seat, action set, alternative rule and the 15-word minimum for every parsed spot, and the parsed count equals the raw count. Holdout: all 110 spots rebuilt independently with createHand/applyAction/playerView using my own deal order. Seat, toAct, hole cards, players, actions, currentBet, betCount and legalActions all equal the validator's view; the recorded action is legal in each view.

The acceptance test covers all four cases with startsWith on 'Golden spot probe: ...'. Holdout, on my own valid 6-max spot: missing id gives '#1: missing id'; missing seats or holeCards gives the matching 'missing player view (...)'; missing position or situation gives '<undefined> does not match the view (CO)' or '(raise-and-calls)'; a missing action, missing justification or two alternatives each give the exact spec text; an illegal step 3 'check' or step 2 'bet' gives 'step k "x" is not legal'. Every message names the spot.

npm test output lists tests/golden/preflop.acceptance.test.ts (118 tests). The AC#2 test checks the test script, the include glob and the sweeps exclusions. In a scratch copy with one broken spot, npm test exited 1 with that spot's message. CI sweep shard 2 ran the file.

There are 110 per-spot tests titled with the id, all passing. Holdout: recommend(view).action equals the recorded action for every spot on my independently rebuilt views. Runner messages on a call spot: 'expected raise, got call', 'expected raise or fold, got call', null when the alternative matches, and a stub advise returning fold gives 'expected call, got fold'. The end-to-end mutation produced the exact message.

110 spots: heads-up 20, 6-max 42, full ring 48. Every (size, situation) in APPLICABLE_SPOTS has at least 4 spots. Actions: raise 48, call 36, fold 22, check 4. Positions covered: heads-up BTN/BB; 6-max all 6; full ring all 9.

The acceptance AC#5 test passes; disabling the borderline check makes it fail. Holdout: a spot on the 6-max CO unopened borderline cell (22) is rejected with the exact message. A chart copy that marks a shipped spot's cell borderline makes parseGoldenSpots throw exactly that one problem.

I checked the engine explanation and justification of all 110 spots with my own sentence splitter (a scan for .!? followed by whitespace or end) and my own whole-word concept matcher over CONCEPTS terms. Every text has 1 to 3 sentences, each ends in punctuation, and each names a concept: 0 failures.

The DoD#1 acceptance test passes: ids and justifications are unique and each justification names its hand. Manual read of about 25 justifications: they are written for each spot, state the hand, price or range reasoning, and show no copied passages. The most similar pair (6max-btn-unopened-k5s and fr-btn-unopened-k4s, similarity ratio 0.81) shares phrasing but differs, which D-3 allows. Chart-neighbour review of all 110 cells: 89 have every same-region neighbour on the same action, and 19 differ only on one edge (mostly the top of a region, such as AKo raise next to AQo call). Two are call islands; see J-1-01.

The unit 'golden spot validator' tests pass and assert exact problem texts for every listed case. Holdout boundaries: a 14-word justification is rejected and a 15-word one accepted; exactly 3 sentences pass and 4 are rejected; untrusted text is cut at 20 characters plus '...'; several problems on one spot are all listed. The sentence-limit and array-alternative mutants are killed by these tests.

The unit 'golden spot views' tests pass (6-max BTN facing a raise: seat 1, currentBet 8, betCount 2, fold/call/raise; heads-up BTN; 9-seat BTN after 6 folds; a BB hero gets its own cards). Actual: two call spots sit on call islands, where both same-region neighbours fold. In fr-co-limpers-87s, 97s and 86s fold. In fr-sb-unopened-65s, 75s and 64s fold, and an SB complete against a raise is arguably a close choice. Neither cell is borderline, and both justifications are sound poker, so the validator rule (AC#5) holds.
